verdict.rationale: Clerk documents a broad programmatic surface: a published OpenAPI spec, a Backend API used for user creation and duplicate-user merging, personal access tokens for that API, and custom flows that reproduce the prebuilt sign-in UI (including MFA via `needs_second_factor`). Its pricing also pairs "APIs and prebuilt UIs" for sign-up, sign-in and profile, and the MCP server and CLI expose account tools to create applications, manage users and set up production. However, nothing claims or demonstrates full parity between the UI/Dashboard and the API, and a hands-on report says parts of the frontend API are sparsely documented, requiring an undocumented key for a token workflow. missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity claim, evidence that all Dashboard configuration is API-accessible, complete frontend API documentation, independent corroboration of parity.
